summary:
I've been building Keikochō, a Japanese-learning app I use myself, and this stretch was mostly about honesty in what the app claims to teach versus what it actually reinforces. I measured how much variety the conversation personas actually offer — turns out with a 12-option question menu, one persona answered "like" to literally every single question, 12 for 12. The fix wasn't more content, it was rekeying personality to a shared semantic space so an answer can't fall through to a generic default. I also found that the app's practice mode had quietly shipped a section with no illustration for three weeks because a list of section IDs grew from three to four and nothing checked that the image folder grew with it — nobody's fault, just a guard that didn't exist. Added a test that would have caught it.

On the image generation side, I've been using Flux and a fine-tuned illustration model (via Replicate) to draw the deck art, and spent real time on failure modes that are specific to diffusion models: it can't count reliably past six without a shape to anchor to ("seven balls in a row" versus "two rows of four and three" — the second one it just gets wrong), it can't draw two people having a conversation without inventing a romance, and naming something you don't want in the image ("no chopsticks standing up in the rice bowl") often causes the model to draw exactly that. The fix each time was rephrasing to describe the positive scene rather than list prohibitions.

Separately, on the infrastructure side I run for personal AI projects, I put together a small monitoring pattern I keep reusing: a handful of background health checks (backups, network mounts, model server heartbeats) that each report one line into a daily status message. The interesting bug there was realizing that "populated" and "fresh" are different failure states — a data sync that's been silently failing for weeks still leaves old files sitting in place, so a plain existence check passes while the data quietly rots. Only checking the file's age catches it.

highlights.oneLiner: Fixed a stance profile that answered like to 12/12 questions by rekeying to shared semantics
Debugging diffusion failure modes: counting past six, two-person scenes, negative prompts
Caught a section that shipped with no illustration for three weeks; added a coverage guard
Built reusable health-check pattern distinguishing populated-but-stale from truly fresh
